dataset.name: Olist Brazilian e-commerce orders
dataset.description: Orders placed on Olist, a Brazilian online marketplace that connects small sellers to customers. Each order has its items, payments, delivery dates and customer review score.

overview.title: What Olist is
overview.text: Olist is a Brazilian e-commerce company that lets small and medium-sized shops sell on large online marketplaces under a single contract. A customer buys on a marketplace, Olist passes the order to the shop that sells the product (the seller), the seller packs it and hands it to a carrier, and the carrier delivers it to the customer anywhere in Brazil. This dataset is a real, anonymised extract of those orders, published by Olist for research and learning.

overview.title: The life of one order
overview.text: Each order belongs to one customer and has one or more items. Every item is one product from one seller, with its own price and freight charge. The order records when it was bought, when the payment was approved, when the seller handed it to the carrier, when it reached the customer, and the delivery date promised at purchase, so the data shows how long each stage took and whether the promise was kept. After delivery the customer can review the order with a score from one to five stars (the review text itself is not in the data).

overview.title: What you can learn from it
overview.text: Sales: revenue and orders by month, category, state, seller and payment type, and the average order value. Delivery: how often orders arrive late, how long seller handling and carrier transit take, and where late orders concentrate. Customers: where they live and how many come back. Reviews: how scores move, and how they differ between late and on-time orders. For a bad month, an investigation compares it with the other months and shows where the change happened.

overview.title: Things to know before you ask
overview.text: Customers and sellers appear only as ids with their city and state: there are no names. Money is in Brazilian reais (R$); revenue counts item prices of orders that were not canceled or unavailable, and freight is reported separately. The data is thin in its first and last months (see the timeline), so trends use the steady months in between, and "today" means the end of the data. Payments can be by credit card (often in installments), boleto (a Brazilian bank slip), voucher or debit card.

overview.title: How the agent answers
overview.text: Each question becomes one read-only SQL query over the six tables below, or a fixed set of queries for an investigation. The query is checked before it runs, the result is computed by the database, and every number in the written answer is traced back to that result. The Evidence tab of each answer shows the exact SQL. The data shows what happened and where; it cannot show why.

views.name: data_coverage
views.description: One row per month: number of orders, whether the month is partial, and whether it is inside the analysis window.

column_notes.is_partial: Fewer than 500 orders in the month: results need a warning.

views.name: order_items
views.description: One row per item in an order: product, category, seller, price and freight.

column_notes.price: Item price, excluding freight. Revenue = sum(price) where is_sale.
column_notes.category: English category; unknown if missing; Portuguese name if untranslated.

views.name: orders
views.description: One row per order: customer, status, purchase and delivery dates, lateness, delivery stages, revenue, freight, payment total and review score.

column_notes.customer_unique_id: The person. Use this, not a per-order id, to count customers.
column_notes.purchase_month: First day of the purchase month (order month).
column_notes.is_sale: True unless status is canceled or unavailable. Revenue counts sales only.
column_notes.is_delivered: Status delivered and a customer delivery timestamp exists.
column_notes.is_late: Delivered date later than estimated date (dates, not timestamps). NULL if not delivered.
column_notes.days_late: Delivered date minus estimated date; negative = early. NULL if not delivered.
column_notes.seller_handling_days: Carrier hand-off minus purchase, in days. NULL if missing or negative.
column_notes.carrier_transit_days: Customer delivery minus carrier hand-off, in days. NULL if missing or negative.
column_notes.promised_days: Estimated delivery date minus purchase, in days.
column_notes.delivery_days: Customer delivery minus purchase, in days.
column_notes.seller_count: Distinct sellers in the order; >1 means a multi-seller order.
column_notes.items_revenue: Sum of item prices, excluding freight; 0 if the order has no items.
column_notes.freight_total: Sum of item freight; never part of revenue.
column_notes.payment_total: Sum of payments; NULL if the order has no payment row.
column_notes.review_score: Score (1-5) of the latest answered review; NULL if not reviewed.

views.name: payments
views.description: One row per order: payment total, number of payments, installments and payment types.

column_notes.payment_types: Distinct payment types joined with +, e.g. credit_card+voucher.
column_notes.primary_payment_type: Payment type of the largest payment row.

views.name: reviews
views.description: One row per order: the latest review score and whether it has a comment (the comment text itself is not available).

views.name: sellers
views.description: One row per seller: seller id, city and state (no seller names).

definitions.definition: January 2017 to August 2018 (data_coverage.in_analysis_window). Data outside it is sparse. When it applies: trends, monthly series, month-to-month comparisons, and per-month averages use only months inside the window (also when the question names a longer period, for example "average orders per month in 2018" uses January to August 2018). Totals and "overall" figures do not apply the window: they use all data in the period the question asks for, or all data if no period is given (for example, the overall late-delivery rate uses every delivered order; revenue in 2016 uses all of 2016).
2018-08-31. Relative dates ("last month", "this year") are resolved against this date, so "last month" means July 2018.
Month of the purchase timestamp.
A month with fewer than 500 orders. Results for it carry a warning. November 2016 has zero orders.
Brazilian reais (BRL, R$). Assumed; the source does not state it.
order_status = 'delivered' and a customer delivery timestamp exists.

A delivered order whose delivery date is later than its estimated delivery date. Dates are compared, not timestamps, because the estimate is always midnight: comparing timestamps would wrongly mark same-day deliveries as late. NULL for orders that are not delivered.
A delivered order that is not late.
Late orders divided by delivered orders. Never divide by all orders.
Delivery date minus estimated date, in days. Negative means early. NULL if not delivered.
Carrier hand-off timestamp minus purchase timestamp, in days (fractional).
Customer delivery timestamp minus carrier hand-off timestamp, in days.
Estimated delivery date minus purchase timestamp, in days.
Customer delivery timestamp minus purchase timestamp, in days.
A stage duration below zero is a recording error (166 orders were handed to the carrier before purchase; 23 were delivered before hand-off). Such durations are NULL.
An order whose status is not canceled or unavailable.
Sum of item price over sales, excluding freight. Including canceled and unavailable orders would change 2017 revenue by 0.77%.
Sum of item freight_value. Reported separately, never inside revenue.
Sum of payment rows for an order. One row per order in payments, so joining it never multiplies item rows.
Revenue divided by the number of sale orders that have items.
A person: customer_unique_id. Never customer_id, which is created per order.
A customer with more than one order. About 3% of customers.
English category name. Products without a category are unknown. The two categories without an English translation keep their Portuguese names.
Score of the latest answered review for the order (one per order). Review text is never available.
A seller or group needs at least 30 orders to appear in a ranking; the sample size is always shown.
An order with items from more than one seller (1,278 orders). Order-level outcomes such as lateness are not attributed to a single seller without saying so.
The pooled value over all other months in the analysis window, excluding the period under investigation.

questions: What was the monthly revenue in 2018?
What is the average order value by payment type?
How is the late-delivery rate trending?
Which states have the highest late-delivery rate?
Why was March 2018 so bad for deliveries?
How many customers placed more than one order?
Which 5 states have the most customers?
Which 5 sellers had the most orders in 2018?
Which seller states have the highest average review score?
How does the review score differ for late and on-time orders?
What share of reviews are 1-star by month?
Which categories have the highest freight cost per item?
How many distinct products were sold in 2017?

limits: No names: sellers and customers are identified by ids, city and state only.
No profit or costs: revenue is item prices; freight is reported separately.
No review text: only scores and whether a comment exists.
No forecasts or predictions: the data describes 2016 to 2018 only.
No causes: the data shows where and when something happened, not why.
No changes: the agent can only read the data, never modify it.

missing_fields.closest: review scores and whether a review has a comment
order status, such as canceled orders
payment types, including vouchers as a payment type
